title: Armamentarium Turcico-Diabolicum (Olaus Fielkius Crone)
shelf_note: A Danish author's Latin occasional poem against the Turks, dedicated to the Duke of Württemberg. It has no tradition and no collection. Its only esoteric touch is the 'conjunctio ... septem Planetarum' omen on p.4. It is in period, but no shelf claims it.
structure_note: 18 records, 18 with OCR, 16 translated. No printed page numbers; signatures A2 and A3 on pp.3 and 5 run in order. Nothing stands out.

title: De natura daemonum libri 4. Io. Laurentii Ananiae Tabernatis theologi
shelf_note: D'Anania's 1581 demonology is a Latin early-modern treatise and sits well in a European libraries collection and in this library's occult/theological scope.
structure_note: 279 pages, all with OCR, 272 translated. 8 backsteps and 32 repeats over 232 printed numbers. The three pages here run 22, 23, 24 in sequence, so the backsteps are more likely misread numerals or front-matter and index numbering than a broken scan. The scan is Google Books ('Digitized by Google').

tr_errors.english: ral fall, they were cast down. For since they did not desire the light of grace, they remained in their own darkness ... having rejected the order of divine love and replaced it with an insatiable hunger for their own exaltation.

structure_note: 498 records, 291 with a printed number, 58 backsteps and 162 repeats. The scan photographs openings and is foliated (one number per leaf, recto only), so versos carry no number and the OCR invents one. Here p.389 is tagged page-num 71 and p.390 page-num 70, which manufactures a backstep. The structure counts are therefore mostly an artefact of foliation plus invented numbers, not a broken scan.
